sources.finding: Publication and body explicitly identify Lord Lasike as Speaker administering member oaths on Friday morning 14 January 2011. This is an office attestation, not a royal appointment date.
The 4 April notice styles Lasike Speaker in announcing the planned 7 April Knesset visit. It supports identity as styled on the notice date; it does not prove the future visit occurred.

The 24 February article, textual photo captions and delegation list identify Tu’ivakano as Speaker. The trip is described as recent and later dated 10–18 February; the packet correctly uses the article as a dated office observation, not a tenure start.

The 18 January article names Lord Speaker Fakafanua among those sworn that day and separately calls Tu’ilakepa Deputy Speaker. This supports the oath event without replacing royal appointment or establishing a tenure start.
The 5 March article names Fakafanua as Speaker addressing the first sitting in the temporary chamber after Gita. It supports that point attestation, not an appointment or first day in the office.
